front.title: MAP Operations: Governance, Registries, Federation, Interoperability, and Migration

abstract.t: This document is part of the MAP (Manolito Agent Protocol) specification family. See draft-map-index-01 for the family overview and reading order.

section.name: Requirements Language
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document family are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174] when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here. No adaptation or weakening of these terms applies.

section.name: Scope
section.t: Everything that keeps the MAP family coherent over time: the engineering policy binding the documents together, code-point registries and their change policies, the deprecation process, federation between meshes, conformance and interoperability testing, the formal-analysis program, reference-implementation guidance, migration from legacy designs, and regulatory notes.

section.name: Engineering policy: bounded contexts and data semantics
section.t: The document family is a deliberate bounded-context decomposition. Each document owns a vocabulary, a small set of aggregates, and explicit data semantics; cross-context references are by identity only (AgentID, TaskID, quote-id, invoice-id, descriptor-cid, transcript-root), never by embedded foreign structures. Context integration happens through signed messages and translation (gateways, §5), never shared internal models.

section.t: Binding rules across the family (restating what each document enforces locally, so reviewers can check any change against one list):

ol.li: One source of truth per fact, named explicitly; everything else is

section.t: a derived copy with a repair path (republish, re-fetch, recompute).

ol.li: Events are past-tense facts (RECEIPT, PAY_RECEIPT, REVOKE);

section.t: commands are requests (ASSIGN, CANCEL, PAY_AGREE); the two are never conflated in naming or semantics.

ol.li: Idempotency everywhere delivery is uncertain: TaskID, invoice-id,

section.t: msg-id, content addresses. No handler MAY have unrepeatable side effects; no design MAY assume exactly-once delivery.

ol.li: Ordering is scoped, never global — and each scope is written down.
Distinguish accepted / durable / applied (visible in pay §1's

section.t: agreed/submitted/settled and tasks' countersigned-checkpoint boundary).

ol.li: Schema evolution is additive within a major version; contract

section.t: changes ride registries and version negotiation; fields are never reused with new meaning (registry policy forbids re-assignment, §3.3).

ol.li: Projections MUST be rebuildable (trust scores from receipts, DHT

section.t: index from descriptors) and their staleness observable.
Changes to any MAP document that violate a row or rule above MUST be rejected in review or accompanied by an explicit amendment to this table.

section.name: Registries and change control
section.t: Registries are documents plus process — never runtime services (arch G1).

section.name: Designated experts
section.t: Two or more per registry, appointed by the project's steering process; review criteria: no semantic overlap with existing points, complete specification, security considerations present.

section.name: Private/experimental use
section.t: Private ranges (core §5, ext keys ≥ 0xF000) require no registration and MUST NOT appear in public-mesh descriptors.

section.name: Immutability of assignments
section.t: Code points are never reused or re-defined; deprecation marks them reserved forever (rule 6 above). As a standing example, message type 0x0206 is a permanent, deliberately-unassigned reservation in the Tasks range (wire §3.20): it is never reused for any future meaning, and any document or implementation that claims 0x0206 is non-conformant.

section.name: Deprecation process
section.t: Mark deprecated in registry with rationale and replacement → minimum two minor versions of dual support → removal only at a major version, with the major's migration notes. HELLO negotiation makes the sunset observable in the field (peers advertising deprecated versions are countable).

section.name: Registry stewardship and IETF submission
section.t: The MAP family is intended for publication as Independent Stream Internet-Drafts (each draft's submissiontype: independent front-matter records this). This section fixes who owns the registries and how governance works — both before and after publication — so the family is externally submittable without an undefined "steering process".

ul.li: Pre-publication ownership. While the documents are Internet-Drafts (not

section.t: yet RFCs), the protocol steward — the document editor(s) named on the front matter of this operations document — is the registry authority. The steward appoints the designated experts required by §3.1, resolves registry disputes, and runs the change-control process in §3/§4. "The project's steering process" (§3.1) means this steward appointment, not a separate body.

ul.li: Post-publication ownership. On IETF publication, IANA operates every

section.t: registry under the policies enumerated in draft-map-wire-01.md §4 (Specification Required, Expert Review, Standards Action). The designated experts become IANA-appointed Expert Reviewers / registration reviewers per the relevant IANA policy; the Independent Stream shepherd and the IESG provide the oversight the stream defines. The MAP steward's pre-publication appointments SHOULD be carried forward as IANA's initial expert roster.

ul.li: Authority split (no double authority). Internal ops §3/§4 change-control

section.t: governs draft revisions and the working tree. Once an RFC is published, code-point assignments are made by IANA under the registered policy; the steward no longer unilaterally assigns points. The immutability and deprecation rules (§3.3/§3.4) apply identically in both periods — IANA honors "never reuse" as a permanent reservation.

ul.li: Intellectual property. The source working tree is distributed under

section.t: Apache-2.0 (see repository README). Contributors SHOULD disclose relevant IPR per IETF BCP 79. The published RFC is copyrighted by the IETF Trust and licensed for use per the IETF Trust's terms; this is distinct from the source-repo Apache-2.0 grant and does not change the wire format or code points.

ul.li: Readiness gate. Submission (and any request that IANA create the

section.t: registries) is gated on the two-independent-implementation criterion in §6.1; the documents remain in draft pending human/expert review until that gate is met and the Independent Stream review completes.

section.name: Versioning discipline
section.t: Semantics per core §6.4. Additionally: every published draft revision carries a changelog distinguishing editorial / additive / breaking; breaking items MUST name the major version that will carry them. Reference implementations MUST keep a compatibility test pinning the previous minor's golden vectors.

section.name: Federation
section.t: A mesh is a deployment sharing bootstrap and policy (arch §3). Meshes federate through gateways — ordinary agents advertising map:cap:gateway/<namespace> — which are, precisely, anti-corruption layers: they translate a foreign context (another mesh, or an external service such as a hosted-model API) into local MAP vocabulary without letting the foreign model leak through.
Gateway rules:

ul.li: G-1: A gateway signs everything as itself. It MUST NOT fabricate

section.t: descriptors, receipts, or proofs purporting to originate from the external party; provenance (gateway-of: <namespace> ext field) is REQUIRED on re-advertised capabilities.

ul.li: G-2: Evidence about work done through a gateway accrues to the gateway's

section.t: AgentID — it is accountable for its upstream, which is exactly the incentive alignment wanted from the "OpenRouter gateway peer" pattern (design3, adopted).

ul.li: G-3: Zone labels never launder through a gateway (arch Z2); a gateway

section.t: bridging to an external API is Zone ≥2 by definition unless the deployment allowlists it into Zone 1.
mesh-registered; collisions resolve in favor of the DNS anchor.
Cross-mesh identity, receipts, and payments need no translation — they are already self-certifying — so federation cost is limited to discovery bridging and policy reconciliation.

section.name: Paid-API gateways (the x402 composition)
section.t: A gateway MAY front an external HTTP service that prices its requests with x402 (pay §5.1: HTTP 402 + X-PAYMENT header; the loop is appropriate exactly here, at the gateway boundary — never between MAP peers). Such a gateway participates in two independent payment legs:

ul.li: Downstream (MAP leg): the gateway is an ordinary MAP payee. It

section.t: quotes, agrees, invoices, and settles under pay §2–§5 with any method and terms it chooses; its price is local policy (a margin over its upstream cost is typical and is nobody else's business — C5).

ul.li: Upstream (rail leg): the gateway is an x402 HTTP payer, spending

section.t: its own funds from its own wallet against the external service's 402 challenge.
Rules (extending G-1..G-4 to money):

ul.li: G-5 — payment legs never launder. The gateway settles each leg in

section.t: its own name and MUST NOT re-present one leg's artifacts as the other's: an upstream x402 settlement is not a MAP PayProof, and a MAP PayProof is never forwarded upstream. Upstream payment evidence (settlement response, tx ref) MAY be embedded in the gateway's signed transcript as gateway-attested evidence — provenance G-1 applies: it is the gateway's statement, not the upstream's.

ul.li: G-6 — spend order. The gateway MUST admit the task (G-3/scope) and

section.t: SHOULD hold its downstream settlement (RECOMMENDED: terms 1 prepaid, pay §5.2.2 — the execution gate is exactly the credit-risk boundary) before initiating any upstream payment. A gateway MUST NOT spend upstream on a task it has rejected or will reject.

ul.li: G-7 — bounded upstream spend. The gateway MUST enforce a per-task

section.t: ceiling on upstream payment; a 402 challenge demanding more is refused fail-closed (the task fails; no payment is made). Upstream price changes never propagate implicitly into an already-agreed MAP quote — the quote is binding (pay §3); the margin absorbs or the gateway eats the loss and reprices future quotes.

ul.li: Retry safety: upstream authorizations SHOULD be derived

section.t: deterministically per (task, attempt) so an HTTP retry cannot double-pay (the same single-use authorization re-presents; the rail's nonce rule dedups) — the same construction as the pay §5.1 invoice nonce, under a distinct domain string.
Compliance (§9) attaches to the gateway as rail participant on the upstream leg and as method operator counterparty on the downstream leg; neither is compliance-free.

section.name: Structure
section.t: Per conformance class (arch §10): golden test vectors (encode/decode/ verify — TV-001/002 seed the set), negative vectors, state-machine conformance suites, and live pairwise interop matrices. Advancement rule: no document leaves draft status without two independent implementations passing the full matrix against each other.

Status (TASK-020, 2026-07-13): the live pairwise matrix is delivered — 16/16, Rust (map-rs) ↔ Go (map-go). Both implementations complete real MAP sessions against each other over framed TCP, in both orientations (each side as dialer and as listener), across 8 scenarios: echo, replay (1003), sequence gap (1003), tamper (2000), cross-session relay (2000 — the live §7.3 anti-relay property), version-disjoint handshake (1001), foreign-SessionID rejection (1006, core §6.1), and delegated handshake with accountable-root resolution (identity §4/§6). The record, toolchain versions, and reproduction driver are in interop/MATRIX.md. This is the substantive session-layer matrix; live cross-language task/receipt/payment flows layer on the same session (I2) and remain future work.

section.name: Required negative tests (minimum)
section.t: Duplicate delivery of every idempotent message (ASSIGN, RECEIPT, PAY_INVOICE, PAY_PROOF) — observable effect exactly once. Replayed envelopes within and across sessions (MUST fail 1003; cross-session MUST fail channel binding). Out-of-order and gapped seq/chunk-seq. Truncated/duplicate-key/indefinite-length CBOR (MUST fail 1000). Stale descriptor seq (MUST NOT regress). Wrong-shard provider records (MUST be discarded). Delegation chains that widen scope/zone/depth (MUST fail 2003). Signature over re-serialized rather than received bytes (vector constructed to differ — MUST fail). Projection rebuild: delete trust scores, recompute from receipt store, byte-compare decisions; same for DHT index from descriptors.

section.name: Formal analysis program
section.t: Delivered for P1–P3 (TASK-014, 2026-07-10). ProVerif 2.05 models at formal/ (repo root): hello-cb.pv (P1 downgrade resistance via the negotiation-recheck + transcript hash, core §6.2; P2 channel-binding session separation, core §7.3 — no two distinguishable sessions ever derive the same CB) and delegation.pv (P3 delegation-chain attenuation is tighten-only, identity §4 / TASK-010 validate_chain, including fail-closed unknown caveats). Adversary: full active Dolev-Yao network control plus a fully compromised insider (a legitimate registered agent's private key is leaked). All three properties hold in the honest models (no counterexample found) and each carries a mandatory negative control that fails with a concrete witnessing trace, proving the queries are not vacuous. No BLOCKING finding. Full methodology, the property-to-spec mapping, and the abstraction gaps (msg-id/timestamp replay cache, sequence numbers, suite negotiation, chain depth bounded to 2 links, zone attenuation, exporter modeled at exactly the strength of the deployed /map/1.0.0 binding per TASK-012 FR-4) are in formal/README.md; captured tool output is under formal/results/.

Remaining future formal work (not yet modeled): receipts non-repudiation, the payment binding chain (quote→agree→invoice→proof), reservation obligations, and the msg-id replay cache itself (closing the Q2 gap noted above to a stronger injective session-uniqueness property). Claims not covered by models or tests are labeled assumptions (arch §7).

section.name: Fuzzing and load
section.t: Continuous structure-aware CBOR fuzzing of every decoder; churn simulation (30 %/hour peer turnover) against discovery; hot-key load tests validating the §6-discovery sharding math at 10^5 synthetic providers per capability.

section.name: From legacy Manolito/MP2P (conceptual)
section.t: No wire compatibility (arch non-goal). Concept map: file-hash search → capability-key lookup; flat UDP peer exchange → Kademlia + AutoNAT/relay; unsigned cleartext → signed CBOR over encrypted transports; "who has the file" results → descriptors + status. The retained virtues are architectural: no supernodes, tolerance of churn, small messages.

section.name: Coexistence
section.t: A HEP-0.1 prototype bridges via a gateway (G-1..G-4) during transition; dual-stack nodes advertise both and prefer MAP sessions.

section.name: Reference implementation guidance
section.t: Rust first (rust-libp2p maturity), Go second; workspace mirrors the context map — one crate per bounded context, dependencies only along the document dependency graph, no shared "common domain" crate beyond identifier newtypes:
section.sourcecode: map/ crates: map-identity, map-core, map-discovery, map-tasks, map-trust, map-pay adapters/ ollama-provider, gateway (hosted-API bridge), ide-rpc storage/ append-only receipt log + rebuildable projections; descriptor cache keyed (AgentID, seq) conformance/ golden vectors, negative vectors, matrix harness
section.t: Implementation musts drawn from §2: value types for AgentID/TaskID/Amount (no bare byte-strings crossing APIs); receipt ingestion idempotent; projection rebuild as a first-class CLI operation; observability for lag (descriptor staleness, credit exhaustion, retry counts, dispute rates). MVP ordering (adapted from design3's scope, which was sound): core + identity handshake → descriptor publish/fetch → echo task with streaming and flow credit → receipts → payments last.

The reference-implementation program is executed through implementation-specification packages in the repository's tasks/ directory (see tasks/README.md): an architect role authors complete, self-contained engineering specifications; coding agents implement them; each package carries its own acceptance criteria and validation checklist, and the spec-feedback rule of §2 (patch the spec in the same change when implementation exposes ambiguity) binds every package. The Rust workspace map-rs/ (impl #1 toward the §6.1 two-implementation rule) is the first target of this process.

Status (TASK-001..003): the map-rs/ scaffold builds and its full test suite is green. The conformance/map-conformance crate reproduces TV-001 and TV-002 byte-for-byte from the seeds and rejects the §6.2 negative catalog (N1–N10), satisfying the §6.2 minimum negative suite for impl #1; the deterministic-CBOR encoder reproduced the cbor2-canonical vectors without modification. Adapter seams (ollama-provider, gateway) and the map-cli tool (keygen, projection rebuild) exist; live transport, delegation, and payments remain future work per the MVP ordering above.

Status (TASK-015, 2026-07-11): impl #2 is at frozen-vector parity. map-go/ (Go, zero external deps, written from the drafts and vectors under the independence rule — no Rust source consulted) reproduces every frozen positive vector byte-for-byte from seeds (TV-001..015 incl. TV-010b; TV-007 ASSIGN is produce+consume in Go, closing that ERRATA parity hole on the Go side), consumes them from frozen bytes, and rejects NV-001..008 with the required classes, including the §6.2 canonicality-vs-signature isolation case (NV-003) and scope-widening delegation (NV-007 → 2003). Strict Ed25519 verification (canonical A/R/S, small-order rejection) is implemented and tested per TASK-015 §FR-4. The live pairwise interop MATRIX (two implementations against each other over a real transport) remains future work — vector parity alone does not advance any document out of draft.

section.name: Compliance and regulatory notes (informative)
section.t: Receipts and descriptors are pseudonymous personal data under GDPR-like regimes: holders are controllers of their local stores; the protocol compels no publication, and erasure is satisfiable because disclosure is pull-based and local deletion is always possible (trust §4). Payment compliance (KYC/AML/sanctions) attaches to settlement methods and their operators (pay §7). Model-output liability and content policy are application-layer; SecurityProfile and zones give deployments the enforcement hooks. Export-control considerations for cryptography follow the chosen suite's primitives, all of which are widely published standards.

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: Governance capture is the meta-risk: registries use open policies with appealable expert review; no registry is a runtime dependency, so capture degrades coordination, not operation. Federation gateways concentrate trust by construction — G-1/G-2 make that concentration visible and priced rather than hidden.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document defines the registration policies and change-control model for the MAP registries (§3), but requests no IANA action of its own: the registries and their initial contents are defined by the protocol documents, and the consolidated index is draft-map-wire-01. Should the family be adopted onto a stream that uses the IANA registries, the policies in §3 (open / Specification Required, with appealable expert review) are the requested assignment policies for each registry named there.
